blocks.heading: Education Loan Secured or Unsecured
rows: Up to ₹4 lakh
No security and no margin money (your own share of the fee). Banks are told not to ask for collateral at this size.
Usually a parent or guardian signs with you as co-borrower.
Unsecured in plain words
₹4 lakh to ₹7.5 lakh
Usually a third-party guarantee and no property. The credit guarantee scheme below can remove even the guarantee.
Parent as co-borrower, plus a guarantor who agrees to repay if the borrowers do not.
Unsecured, but a named person must repay if you cannot
Above ₹7.5 lakh
Property or a fixed deposit of enough value, such as a house, a plot or a bank deposit.
Parent as co-borrower, and the pledged asset.
Secured

blocks.heading: Route to Try First
rows: You have a merit seat at an institution on the PM-Vidyalaxmi list
PM-Vidyalaxmi, applied for through a bank or the Vidya Lakshmi portal
The co-borrower's income and credit record. No property and no guarantor.
The gap is up to ₹7.5 lakh and the family has no property to offer
A bank loan that carries the government credit guarantee
The co-borrower's income and credit record. The guarantee takes the place of security.
The gap is above ₹7.5 lakh and the college has a strong, checked record
An unsecured offer from a bank or NBFC, priced against a secured one
A higher rate, stricter checks on the co-borrower and their credit record.
The gap is above ₹7.5 lakh and only a secured loan is on offer
The secured loan, but only after the rupee check and a lower-cost college comparison
The pledged house, plot or deposit.

items.text: The bank holds a claim on your asset until the loan is cleared.
The rate is often lower, but the gap can be small, as the rupee check below shows.
